newsitem.title: UK: UK active funds outstrip index trackers yr to Sept.
newsitem.headline: UK active funds outstrip index trackers yr to Sept.

text.p: Actively managed UK equity growth funds have kept pace with their benchmark over the 12 months to September 1, 1996 while index trackers struggled to outperform the market, a report from Fund Research shows.

UK Equity Growth funds rose an average 17.4 percent versus their FTSE All-share index rise of 15.8 percent (offer to offer, income reinvested) while tracker funds rose just 14.2 percent against the All-Share benchmark of 15.8 percent.
Fund Research, an independent company which tracks fund investment strategy and performance worldwide, said political uncertainty had capped gains for the UK Equity Growth sector.
"There is concern about the impact of the Labour Party's domestic economic policies if it wins the general election, particularly adoption of the EU's social chapter."
But most fund managers said the economic environment for the UK remained favourable with low inflation and interest rates seen continuing.
Most funds in the sector are fully invested, Fund Research said, and not specifically orientated towards defensive stocks.

It noted that the UK Equity Growth unit trust sector is now the second largest UK sector with total assets of 18.7 billion stg at the beginning of September compared with 20.5 billion stg for the Growth and Income sector. The Smaller Companies sector accounts for 8.5 billion stg.

The Equity Growth sector has advanced 32 percent since the beginning of the year, but Smaller Companies has leapt 52 percent. Smaller Companies was also the strongest performing sector over the last five years, returning 113.3 percent.
Fund Research said it did not itself track index funds "because there is little the individual fund manager can do to influence relative results outside the benchmark".

But Micropal data showed that in the latest 12 month period, no index funds achieved an identical return with their indices (FTSE 100 and FTSE All Share) and only three exceeded it, one of which was a geared index fund.
"Allowing a possibly generous 1.5 percentage point cost for management and other fees, over the past 12 months 12 out of 20 funds failed to meet their objective," Fund Research said.
Among other observations about the sector, Fund Research looked at average portfolio composition in the UK Growth sector.

"It indicates great diversity from concentrated portfolios (27 stocks) to highly diversified funds (340 stocks), and from managers with high levels of turnover (four recording ratios of over 100 percent) to those with low turnover (six with 20 percent or less)."
